text:
Somebody's bad week ends tonight. Anaheim and Seattle are both 1-4-0 in their last five, the Ducks fourth in the Pacific and the Kraken sixth, two points behind them. Our playoff chances read 42% for Anaheim and 29% for Seattle, which is about as much as a division game in November can move.

The Ducks have the league's hottest scorer and a goaltending problem. Cutter Gauthier has 18 points in his last 10 games, a breakout by our numbers, and he is at 46% to score tonight. His name has also been in the headlines for the way he left Philadelphia: Flyers GM Daniel Briere spent last week publicly disputing a report by Elliotte Friedman about the trade. Mikael Granlund, the captain, has 16 points in 10. The problem is in net. Lukas Dostal is at .838 over his last five starts, 5.4 goals worse than expected, and Anaheim has been outscored 15-8 during a three-game winless run. Beckett Sennecke (26 points in 22 games) and Ryan Poehling are both on injured reserve, which has pushed Troy Terry onto the top power play.

Seattle's bright spot is Berkly Catton, whose first NHL hat trick powered a 5-1 win over Vancouver on Thursday. He has 10 points in 10, though our numbers say bounces have helped. Matty Beniers has goals in three straight games. The worry is the penalty kill: after two power-play goals against in Saturday's 4-3 loss in San Jose, Alison Lukan reported that coach Lane Lambert called it "the elephant in the room." Jared McCann is out until about January. Bobby McMann has no goals in 13 games on 2.8 expected goals, the kind of drought our numbers say the chances don't deserve.

Neither side has controlled play this season, 46% of the expected goals at five on five for Anaheim and 45% for Seattle. Our numbers lean slightly to the Ducks, 3.62 expected goals to 3.23, with Philipp Grubauer, near league average this season, projected for Seattle. Our sleeper is Anaheim's Jeff Malott, a third-liner whose shots have been dangerous, at 14% to score.
headline: Two Pacific teams in a slide meet in Seattle
